paper.title: Salsa20 specification
paper.venue: eSTREAM (ECRYPT stream cipher project) submission document, cr.yp.to/snuffle/spec.pdf

program.how: written for ounce-core from the definitions in the specification; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: the specification's worked examples for quarterround (7 of 7), rowround (2 of 2), columnround (2 of 2), doubleround (2 of 2) and littleendian (3 values) reproduce exactly
the four Salsa20 hash examples reproduce exactly, including the example that iterates the hash one million times (Salsa20^1000000)
the two expansion-function examples reproduce exactly (32-byte key Salsa20_{k0,k1}(n) and 16-byte key Salsa20_k(n))

expected_values_source.what: the numeric examples printed in sections 3 to 9 of the specification, parsed mechanically from the text of the fetched PDF (pdftotext) into the C source, not typed by hand
expected_values_source.note: the examples are data, copied as numbers; the specification contains no code and none was copied from elsewhere

negative_control: built with -DS_ROUNDS=9 (nine double rounds instead of ten), 15 of 20 example groups match (the all-zero hash example and the round-function examples are unaffected), the program prints FAIL and exits 1; check.sh would report NOT REPRODUCED
not_checked: the specification's security claims or any cryptanalysis
the stream-encryption function of section 10 (the specification gives no test vector for it; this check does not run it)
other round counts (Salsa20/8, Salsa20/12) and the eSTREAM test-vector files
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the values the specification prints for its 20 example groups. It does not show the cipher is secure.
